STRONG INDEPENDENT CLOSURE (the single best evidence the burst-window numbers are real): fitting the encoder cost law from the two published points f(1)=8.16 ms, f(64)=316.4 ms gives slope b=4.8927 ms/image and intercept a=3.2673 ms (the text's '~3.2 ms fixed per-forward overhead', exact). Applying it to the window's own published aggregates -- 83,376 forwards (l.353) over 8.3 h (l.250) at 116 img/s (l.250) = 29,880 s and 3,466,080 images -- yields 83,376*3.2673 + 4.8927*3,466,080 = 17,231 s of kernel time against 2 workers x 29,880 s = 59,760 worker-seconds of capacity, i.e. 28.83% utilization. The chapter independently reports 29% mean utilization at lines 340, 361 and 376. Four separately-published quantities close to within 0.6%.

SECOND CLOSURE: at the calibrated steady knee s=2 the encoder load is 16 img/s and 5.54 req/s; kernel demand = 16*4.8927 + 5.54*3.2673 = 96.4 ms/s against 2000 ms/s of capacity = 4.8% (upper bound, since batching cuts the forward count below one-per-request). The chapter states 4.5% (l.297). Consistent.

The extractor assumed the tab:sim-knees arrow reads knee -> successor. It does not: the arrow's first entry is the s=1 value. Proof: the AIC steady row's first entry (307) is bit-identical to tab:sim-poly-aic's AIC TTFT p99 cell, which is an s=1 measurement; and the Vision/steady row's second entry (787) must be the s=32 value because that row is censored and has no successor. Under the correct reading the successor TTFT values are simply not published, so 1.8--2.1x is unverifiable rather than false, and is monotonically consistent with the published sequence 307 (s=1), 418 (s=2), 882 (s=4, l.77). The real defect is the undefined arrow notation (recorded at line 274). (2) '706 vs 651 exceeds 8%' -- CONFIRMED, 8.4485%. (3) '2x decode latency; tok/s convention' -- CONFIRMED as ambiguous, and refined: the 8B's tok/s offset (+12.2% over 1000/TPOT) matches tab:sim-poly-aic's uniform +9% Jensen gap, but the 235B's (+29.7%) does not, so the two models' figures are not on one convention. (4) '249 vs 248' -- CONFIRMED as a genuine text/table contradiction, since the arrow's first entry is the s=1 value, i.e. exactly the quantity tab:sim-poly-aic prints as 248. (5) 'one octave for s=3 -> s=2' -- CONFIRMED, 0.585 octaves. (6) 'factor >10 vs measured 16' -- CONFIRMED as loose. (7) '2,726 images/s vs 370 img/s' -- CONFIRMED as an averaging-window ambiguity on line 251. (8) '4.5% vs 29% utilization' -- REFUTED: these are different windows at different speedups, and both recompute correctly from the chapter's own cost law (4.8% upper bound at steady s=2; 28.8% on the burst window). No defect. (9) 'TP2 margin unbacked' -- the text itself declares the sensitivity run future work, so it is not an internal-consistency defect. (10) 'max TTFT 7.6 vs 4.5 s needs per-request data' -- 4.5 s is internally consistent with tab:sim-poly-aic's 4,518 ms; the 7.6 s value has no internal cross-reference and is not checkable in this pass.

ADDITIONAL FINDING NOT FLAGGED BY THE EXTRACTOR: line 185's '69 batch sizes' across 'the whole $N\le64$ regime' is a cardinality impossibility for distinct integer batch sizes (recorded above).

SUB-THRESHOLD OBSERVATIONS (noted, not itemised): (a) line 147's '~46 s' for a computed 46.52 s rounds the wrong way -- '~47 s' or '46.5 s' would be exact, a 1.1% understatement with no downstream consequence.
